Title: Find Your Main Water Shutoff Valve Before You Need It
Description: Do you know where your main water shutoff valve is? Most homeowners don't until a pipe bursts. Look where the water line enters the house — often in the basement, crawlspace, utility room or near the water heater. Turn it gently to make sure it moves, then hang a bright tag on it so anyone in the family can find it fast. A simple home maintenance habit that can save your floors. More easy home checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: main water shutoff valve, burst pipe, home maintenance tips, winter home prep, plumbing basics, new homeowner tips

Title: Fresh Paint in One Spot? What Home Buyers Should Ask
Description: A whole house freshly painted for sale is normal. A single fresh patch on a ceiling, a basement wall, or under a window is worth noticing. It can be covering an old water stain. Ask the seller what happened there and whether it was repaired, and point it out to your home inspector. One of the easy-to-miss house hunting red flags from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: house hunting red flags, buying a house tips, home inspection, water stain, first time home buyer, home showing tips

Title: Clean Your Dryer Vent — Not Just the Lint Screen
Description: The lint screen catches most of it, but lint still builds up inside the dryer duct and the outside vent. Signs it's clogged: clothes take longer to dry, the dryer feels very hot, or the outside flap barely moves when it runs. Unplug the dryer, disconnect the duct, and clean it with a vent brush, then check the outside flap. Easy home maintenance that keeps your dryer working well. More simple checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: dryer vent cleaning, dryer lint, laundry room, home safety, home maintenance tips, fire prevention

Title: Foundation Cracks — Which Ones Buyers Should Worry About
Description: Not every foundation crack is a problem. Thin vertical hairline cracks are common as concrete cures. Cracks that run horizontally, step diagonally through block, are wider at one end, or have one side pushed out deserve a closer look by a structural engineer before you buy. Take photos and ask the seller what they know. A house hunting tip from Walter's Home Check, with more buyer checks on the page.
Keywords: foundation cracks, house hunting tips, buying a house, home inspection, first time home buyer, structural problems

Title: How to Test Your Sump Pump in 2 Minutes
Description: The worst time to find out your sump pump doesn't work is during a storm. Test it: slowly pour a bucket of water into the sump pit. The float should rise, the pump should switch on, empty the pit and shut off by itself. Check that the discharge pipe outside is clear and drains away from the house. Simple basement waterproofing habit for every season. More basement checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: sump pump test, wet basement, basement waterproofing, home maintenance tips, storm prep, homeowner checklist

Title: Bad Yard Grading — an Easy Red Flag to Spot When House Hunting
Description: Walk all the way around the house you're thinking of buying. The ground right next to the foundation should slope away. Soil, flower beds or patios that slope toward the house send rainwater to the basement walls. Also look at where the downspouts end. It's often fixable, but it tells you to look harder inside for water. More buyer red flags on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: yard grading, foundation drainage, buying a house tips, house hunting checklist, wet basement, home inspection

Title: Water Heater Relief Valve — What to Look For
Description: Every tank water heater has a temperature and pressure relief valve, usually on the top or side, with a pipe running down toward the floor. That pipe should be open at the end, never capped or plugged. Drips, rust or white crust around the valve are worth a plumber's look. While you're there, check the label for the water heater's age. Quick water heater maintenance check from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: water heater maintenance, relief valve, TPR valve, plumbing check, home maintenance tips, water heater safety

Title: Musty Basement Smell — a Red Flag When Buying a House
Description: At a showing, take a deep breath when you walk into the basement. A musty smell usually means moisture. Then look: white chalky deposits on the walls, rust on nails or the water heater base, stains at the bottom of walls, fresh paint low down, and a dehumidifier hard at work. Ask about water history and have it checked. House hunting tips from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: musty basement, wet basement, buying a house tips, house hunting checklist, home inspection, first time home buyer

Title: When to Recaulk Your Bathtub (and Why It Matters)
Description: The caulk line around a tub or shower is a small thing that keeps water out of the wall. Look for gaps, cracks, peeling, or dark spots that won't clean off. If you see them, cut out the old caulk, clean and dry the joint completely, and run a fresh bead of kitchen-and-bath silicone. An easy weekend bathroom maintenance job that protects what's behind the tile. More quick checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: recaulk bathtub, bathroom caulk, shower maintenance, water damage prevention, home maintenance tips, DIY home repair

Title: Old 9x9 Floor Tiles — Why to Test Before You Remove Them
Description: Many older homes have 9-inch square vinyl floor tiles, often in basements and kitchens. Some tiles from that era, and the black adhesive under them, contain asbestos. Intact tiles are usually not a problem; breaking, sanding or scraping them is. Leave them in place or cover them, and have a sample tested before any removal. Check what else to look at for your home's age with Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: asbestos floor tiles, 9x9 tiles, old house renovation, older home problems, basement remodel, house built in

Title: How to Test a GFCI Outlet (a 5-Minute Home Safety Check)
Description: GFCI outlets are the ones with TEST and RESET buttons, usually in kitchens, bathrooms, garages, laundry rooms and outside. Press TEST: the power should cut off with a click. Press RESET to bring it back. If it won't trip or won't reset, have an electrician take a look. Many makers suggest testing them monthly. A quick home safety check anyone can do. More five-minute checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: GFCI outlet test, electrical safety, home maintenance checklist, bathroom outlet, home safety tips, homeowner tips

Title: Ceiling Water Stains — What Buyers Should Ask
Description: A brown ring on a ceiling means water got there at some point. The question is whether it's an old, repaired leak or an active one. Look at what's above it: a bathroom, the roof, an AC unit, a chimney. Ask the seller when it happened and what was fixed, and have your inspector check it, ideally with a moisture meter. House hunting tips from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: ceiling water stain, roof leak, buying a house tips, home inspection, house hunting red flags, first time home buyer

Title: Test Your Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarms (and Check the Date)
Description: Press and hold the test button on every smoke alarm and carbon monoxide alarm in the house. Then take one down and look at the back: most have a manufacture date and the maker says how many years it's good for. Old alarms get replaced, not just new batteries. A two-minute home safety check that's worth putting on the calendar. More easy home safety checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: smoke alarm test, carbon monoxide detector, home safety checklist, fire safety, home maintenance, homeowner tips

Title: Removing a Popcorn Ceiling? Test It for Asbestos First
Description: Popcorn or cottage cheese ceilings were popular for decades, and some applied before the 1980s contain asbestos. You can't tell by looking. Before you scrape, sand or drill it, have a sample tested by a lab. If it's positive, leave it alone or hire a licensed abatement pro. A sensible first step for older home renovations. See what to check for your build year with Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: popcorn ceiling removal, asbestos testing, older home problems, old house renovation, ceiling remodel, house built in

Title: Downspout Extensions — the Easy Fix for a Wet Basement
Description: Watch your downspouts next time it rains. If the water pours out right next to the foundation, it soaks the soil against your basement walls. A simple downspout extension or splash block that carries water several feet away from the house is one of the easiest ways to help keep a basement dry. Check that gutters aren't overflowing too. More rainy-day home checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: downspout extension, wet basement, gutter drainage, foundation water, home maintenance tips, rainy day home check

Title: Signs of DIY Electrical Work to Spot Before You Buy a House
Description: Amateur electrical work is one of the more common things buyers miss. Look for extension cords stapled along walls, junction boxes without covers, loose outlets, outlets or switch plates that feel warm, and lights that flicker. In basements and garages, look for wiring that just doesn't look neat. Point it out to your inspector and consider an electrician's opinion. More buyer red flags on Walter's page.
Keywords: DIY electrical, electrical problems, buying a house tips, house hunting red flags, home inspection, first time home buyer

Title: Check Your Washing Machine Hoses Before They Leak
Description: The rubber hoses behind your washing machine are under water pressure all the time. Pull the machine out a little and look: bulges, cracks, stiffness or rust at the fittings mean it's time to replace them. Braided stainless hoses are a popular upgrade, and it's a good habit to know where the washer's shutoff valves are. A five-minute laundry room check. More quick home checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: washing machine hoses, laundry room, water leak prevention, home maintenance checklist, plumbing tips, homeowner tips

Title: Knob-and-Tube Wiring — How to Spot It in an Older Home
Description: Knob-and-tube wiring was common in houses built roughly before the 1950s. Look in the attic and basement for single wires running on white ceramic knobs and through ceramic tubes. It has no ground wire, and decades of changes and buried insulation can make it a concern. Many insurers ask about it, so have an electrician evaluate it. Check what else to look at for your build year with Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: knob and tube wiring, old house wiring, older home problems, electrical safety, buying an old house, house built in

Title: The Food Coloring Test for a Silent Toilet Leak
Description: A toilet can leak water into the bowl all day without making a sound. Test it: put a few drops of food coloring in the tank, don't flush, and wait about 15 minutes. If color shows up in the bowl, the flapper isn't sealing. Flappers are usually an easy DIY swap. Flush afterward so the color doesn't stain. A simple bathroom check that saves water. More easy home checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: toilet leak test, food coloring test, toilet flapper, save water, bathroom maintenance, DIY plumbing

Title: Buying a Flipped House? Check What They Didn't Fix
Description: Flipped houses can look amazing: new floors, fresh paint, shiny kitchen. Look past it. Check the age of the roof, electrical panel, water heater, furnace and AC, and look at the foundation and attic. Ask for permits on the work that was done, and get your own full home inspection. A beautiful finish doesn't tell you about the systems underneath. Buyer tips from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: buying a flipped house, house flip red flags, buying a house tips, home inspection, first time home buyer, house hunting

Title: How to Tell When Your Furnace Filter Needs Changing
Description: An easy furnace filter check: slide it out and hold it up to a light. If you can barely see light through it, swap it. Match the size printed on the frame and point the airflow arrow toward the furnace. Write the date on the edge so you know when you changed it. A clean HVAC filter helps your system breathe and keeps dust down. Find more quick home maintenance checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: furnace filter, HVAC filter, change air filter, home maintenance checklist, heating system, homeowner tips

Title: Vermiculite Attic Insulation — What Older Home Owners Should Know
Description: Look in the attic of an older home. If the insulation is loose, pebbly and gray-brown or silvery-gold, it may be vermiculite, and some vermiculite contains asbestos. Don't disturb it, don't store things up there, and don't try to remove it yourself. Have it tested and get a pro's advice before any attic work. More era-by-era checks in Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: vermiculite insulation, attic insulation, asbestos, older home problems, old house tips, house built in

Title: Garage Door Auto-Reverse Test Every Family Should Do
Description: Your automatic garage door should reverse if it hits something. Test it: lay a 2x4 flat on the floor under the door and press close. It should touch the board and go back up. Then wave something through the beam of the photo-eye sensors near the floor while it closes; it should stop and reverse. If either test fails, look at the opener manual or call a garage door pro. More simple safety checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: garage door safety, auto reverse test, garage door opener, home safety checklist, home maintenance, family safety

Title: Sticking Doors and Sloping Floors — What They Can Mean
Description: At a showing, open and close every door. One that sticks in summer is usually humidity. Several doors that rub or won't latch, together with sloping floors, diagonal cracks at the corners of doors and windows, or gaps at the top of door frames, can point to movement in the house. It's worth having it looked at before you buy. House hunting tips from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: sticking doors, sloping floors, foundation settling, buying a house tips, home inspection, house hunting red flags

Title: Check Your Yard Grading to Keep Water Away From the Foundation
Description: Good grading means the ground slopes away from your house so rain runs off instead of toward the foundation. Lay a long straight board on the ground pointing out from the wall, put a level on it, and see which way it tips. Low spots and flower beds that slope toward the house can be built back up with soil. An easy outside check for wet basement prevention. More outdoor home checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: yard grading, foundation drainage, wet basement, landscaping slope, home maintenance tips, exterior home check

Title: Aluminum Wiring in 1960s and 1970s Homes — What to Know
Description: Some homes built roughly from the mid-1960s to the mid-1970s have aluminum branch wiring. The concern is the connections at outlets, switches and splices, which can loosen and overheat over time. Look for "AL" printed on wire jackets in the panel or basement, and have an electrician check it; there are proven repair methods. Find more checks for your home's age in Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: aluminum wiring, 1970s house, older home problems, electrical safety, buying an old house, house built in

Title: Disconnect Garden Hoses Before the First Freeze
Description: One of the easiest winter home prep jobs: disconnect, drain and store your garden hoses before the first hard freeze. A connected hose traps water in the outdoor faucet, where it can freeze and crack the pipe inside the wall, and you may not see the leak until spring. If you have an inside shutoff for the faucet, close it and drain the line. Walter's free Before the First Freeze checklist has the rest.
Keywords: winterize outdoor faucet, garden hose, frozen pipes, winter home prep, fall home maintenance, before the first freeze

Title: What to Look For in Your Attic After a Storm
Description: After heavy rain or wind, take a flashlight into the attic (step only on the joists). Look at the underside of the roof for wet spots, dark stains, drips around vents and chimneys, and any daylight coming through. Feel the insulation for damp patches. Catching a small roof leak early is much easier than finding it on the ceiling later. More storm and roof checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: attic inspection, roof leak, storm damage, roof maintenance, home maintenance tips, after storm checklist

Title: How to Check a Water Heater's Age Before You Buy a House
Description: The water heater's manufacture date is usually on the label, sometimes hidden in the serial number (look up the maker's code online). Rust around the base, water in the drain pan, or crust on the relief valve suggest it's near the end. It's not a deal breaker, but it's good to know before you move in. A quick house hunting check from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: water heater age, buying a house tips, home inspection checklist, first time home buyer, house hunting, plumbing check

Title: Polybutylene Pipes — How to Spot Them in Your Home
Description: Polybutylene water pipe was used in many homes built roughly from the late 1970s to the mid-1990s. It's usually gray (sometimes blue or black), flexible, and often stamped PB2110. It has a history of failing without much warning. Look near the water heater, under sinks and where the main line enters. Ask a plumber about it, especially when buying. More checks by build year in Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: polybutylene pipes, 1980s house, plumbing problems, older home problems, buying a house, house built in

Title: Why to Clean Gutters After the Leaves Fall
Description: Clean your gutters once the trees are bare, not just in early fall. Clogged gutters overflow right at the foundation and can help ice dams form along the roof edge in winter. Scoop out the leaves, flush with a hose, and check that each downspout runs clear and empties away from the house. Use a sturdy ladder and a helper, or hire it out. More fall home maintenance tips on Walter's page.
Keywords: gutter cleaning, fall home maintenance, ice dams, winter home prep, downspouts, fall checklist

Title: Look Under Every Sink for a Slow Leak
Description: Slow drips under sinks can go unnoticed for months. Open each cabinet with a flashlight, run the water, and feel the pipes, the shutoff valves and the cabinet floor. Water stains, swollen or soft wood, rust, or a musty smell all point to a leak. Many small leaks are just a loose slip nut. Five minutes, every sink in the house. More quick home maintenance checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: under sink leak, plumbing check, water damage, kitchen sink, home maintenance checklist, homeowner tips

Title: How to Tell If a Roof Is Near the End When Buying a House
Description: Ask the seller how old the roof is and whether there are receipts. Then look for yourself from the ground: curling or cupped shingles, missing pieces, bald spots, granules collecting in the gutters, and patches of different colored shingles. Inside, look for stains on top floor ceilings. A roof near the end of its life is a big item to plan for. More buyer checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: roof age, roof inspection, buying a house tips, house hunting checklist, first time home buyer, home inspection

Title: Lead Paint in Homes Built Before 1978 — Test Before You Sand
Description: Homes built before 1978 may have lead-based paint somewhere under the newer layers. Intact paint is usually left alone; the risk comes from dust and chips when it's sanded, scraped or heat-stripped. Test before a project, using a certified lead inspector or an EPA-recognized test kit, and use lead-safe work practices. See what else to check for your home's build year with Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: lead paint, old house renovation, homes built before 1978, older home problems, home renovation safety, house built in

Title: Test Your Furnace Before the First Cold Day
Description: Don't wait for the first freezing night to find out your heat doesn't work. On a mild fall day, change the filter and run the heat for a while. A slight dusty smell the first time is common. Banging, squealing, a burning smell that doesn't fade, or no warm air means it's time for an HVAC service call, before everyone else calls too. More fall home prep on Walter's page.
Keywords: furnace maintenance, fall home maintenance, heating system, winter home prep, HVAC tips, fall checklist

Title: How to Label Your Breaker Panel (Weekend Home Project)
Description: A breaker panel full of blank or faded labels makes every small problem harder. With a helper and a phone, switch off one breaker at a time and note which lights and outlets go dark. Write clear labels and tape a printed map inside the panel door. Leave the panel cover on and call an electrician for anything inside it. A satisfying weekend home project. More home checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: label breaker panel, electrical panel, circuit breaker, weekend home project, home organization, homeowner tips

Title: Foggy Double-Pane Windows — What Buyers Should Know
Description: If you see fog, haze or water droplets between the two panes of glass, the window's seal has failed. The window still works, but it insulates less and the haze won't clean off. During a showing, count how many windows are affected and look at the frames for rot or water stains. Good to know before you make an offer. More house hunting tips on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: foggy windows, failed window seal, double pane windows, buying a house tips, home inspection, house hunting checklist

Title: Old White Pipe Insulation in the Basement — Leave It Be
Description: In many older homes, heating pipes and boilers are wrapped in white or gray insulation that looks like plaster or corrugated paper. Some of it contains asbestos. If it's intact, it's usually best left alone. If it's damaged, crumbling or in the way of a project, have it tested and handled by a licensed pro. See what else to check for your home's age with Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: asbestos pipe insulation, old boiler, basement pipes, older home problems, old house tips, house built in

Title: How to Keep Pipes From Freezing in a Cold Snap
Description: When a hard freeze is coming: open sink cabinet doors on outside walls so warm air reaches the pipes, let a faucet on an outside wall drip slowly, keep the garage door closed, and don't turn the heat way down if you travel. Know where your main water shutoff is in case a pipe does burst. Walter's free Before the First Freeze checklist covers the rest of winter prep.
Keywords: prevent frozen pipes, winter home prep, cold weather tips, burst pipe, winter home maintenance, homeowner tips

Title: 5 Signs Your Roof Is Near the End of Its Life
Description: How to tell if your roof is getting old, from the ground and the attic: curling or cupped shingles, bald spots and lots of granules in the gutters, missing or cracked shingles, water stains or daylight in the attic, and a sagging ridge. One sign alone may just need a repair; several together mean it's time to get a roofer's opinion and plan ahead. More home checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: roof replacement signs, old roof, roof inspection, home maintenance checklist, roofing tips, homeowner tips

Title: Check Your Fire Extinguisher Gauge (Takes 10 Seconds)
Description: Look at the small pressure gauge on your fire extinguisher: the needle should be in the green. Check that the pin and seal are in place and the hose isn't cracked. Look at the label for the date and the maker's guidance on replacing it. Keep one where you can grab it on the way out of the kitchen, not behind the stove. Quick home safety check from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: fire extinguisher check, kitchen safety, home safety checklist, fire safety tips, home maintenance, family safety

Title: Soft Floor Around the Toilet — a Hidden Leak Red Flag
Description: In every bathroom at a showing, gently press the floor around the toilet and in front of the tub with your foot. It should feel solid. A soft, spongy or bouncy spot, loose tiles, or stains around the base can mean water has been getting under the floor for a while. Check the ceiling below too. An easy house hunting check from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: bathroom floor damage, toilet leak, water damage, buying a house tips, house hunting red flags, home inspection

Title: Galvanized Water Pipes in Older Homes — Signs to Watch For
Description: Galvanized steel water pipes were common in homes built roughly before the 1960s. Over time they can rust and narrow from the inside. Clues: low water pressure, brownish water when a tap is first turned on, and rust at the joints. A magnet sticks to galvanized pipe but not to copper. A plumber can tell you how much life is left. See more checks for your home's age in Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: galvanized pipes, old plumbing, low water pressure, older home problems, old house tips, house built in

Title: Big Icicles on Your Roof? What They Can Tell You About Ice Dams
Description: Big icicles and thick ice along the edge of the roof often mean an ice dam: heat leaks into the attic, melts snow higher up, and the water refreezes at the cold eaves. Water can back up under the shingles. The long-term fixes are usually air sealing and insulation in the attic, and good ventilation. Don't chip at ice from a ladder. More winter home tips on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: ice dams, icicles on roof, attic insulation, winter roof, winter home maintenance, roof leak

Title: 7 Things to Check Before Winter (Easy Winter Home Prep Checklist)
Description: A simple winter home prep checklist: disconnect garden hoses, clean the gutters and downspouts, change the furnace filter, test smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, seal drafts around doors and windows, find your main water shutoff, and check the attic for damp spots. Most take a few minutes. Save it for the weekend before the first freeze, or grab Walter's free Before the First Freeze checklist.
Keywords: winter home checklist, winter home prep, fall home maintenance, winterize house, home maintenance checklist, before the first freeze

Title: The Toilet Paper Test for Your Bathroom Exhaust Fan
Description: A bathroom fan can be noisy and still move very little air. Turn it on and hold a single square of toilet paper up to the grille. It should be pulled up and held there. If not, the fan may be clogged with dust or the duct may be blocked or disconnected. A working bathroom exhaust fan helps keep moisture, peeling paint and mildew down. More easy checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: bathroom exhaust fan, bathroom mildew, moisture control, ventilation, home maintenance tips, bathroom tips

Title: Strong Air Freshener at a Showing? Here's Why to Look Twice
Description: A nice candle at an open house is normal. Strong scents in every room, especially basements and closets, can cover up odors like pet urine, smoke or dampness. Open closet doors and cabinets, smell the basement, and look at carpets and baseboards. If you're serious about the house, visit again at a different time of day. Buyer tips from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: house showing tips, buying a house tips, house hunting red flags, first time home buyer, home inspection, open house tips

Title: Federal Pacific and Zinsco Panels — Why to Check Your Panel's Brand
Description: The brand name is usually on the panel door or the label inside it. Some older panels, including Federal Pacific Electric (Stab-Lok breakers) and Zinsco, have known concerns, and some insurers ask about them. If yours is one of them, or just very old, have a licensed electrician take a look. Leave the cover on yourself. More checks for your home's build year in Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: Federal Pacific panel, Zinsco panel, electrical panel, older home problems, electrical safety, house built in

Title: Get Your Chimney Checked Before the First Fire of the Season
Description: Before you light the first fire of the season, have the chimney inspected and cleaned if needed; creosote builds up inside with use. Check that the damper opens and closes, the chimney cap is in place, and nothing is nesting up there. Keep a screen in front of the fire and the smoke and CO alarms working. More fall home safety checks on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: chimney inspection, fireplace safety, creosote, fall home maintenance, winter home prep, home safety

Title: 6 Things to Check at a House Showing (First-Time Buyer Checklist)
Description: A quick house showing checklist for buyers: look up for ceiling stains, open every sink cabinet, take a deep breath in the basement, run the taps and flush the toilets, find the electrical panel and water heater and check their age, and walk around outside to see which way the ground slopes. Your home inspector goes deeper. Walter's House Buyer's Red Flag Checklist has 50 more.
Keywords: house showing checklist, first time home buyer, buying a house tips, house hunting checklist, home inspection, open house tips

Title: How to Clean Refrigerator Coils (Easy Kitchen Maintenance)
Description: Refrigerator condenser coils collect dust and pet hair, which makes the fridge work harder to stay cold. Unplug it, find the coils (behind a grille at the bottom front or on the back), and vacuum them with a brush attachment or a coil brush. Check your manual for your model. A quick kitchen maintenance job most people never do. More simple home checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: clean refrigerator coils, kitchen maintenance, appliance care, fridge maintenance, home maintenance checklist, cleaning tips

Title: Checking the Furnace and AC When Buying a House
Description: Find the furnace and the outdoor AC unit and look at the data plate for the age (often in the serial number). Look for a service sticker with recent dates and ask the seller for maintenance records. Rust, unusual noises or a unit that won't run in the right season are worth an HVAC technician's opinion before closing. A house hunting check from Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: furnace age, AC unit, HVAC inspection, buying a house tips, first time home buyer, home inspection checklist

Title: Two-Prong Outlets in an Older Home — the Safe Way to Upgrade
Description: Two-prong outlets are common in older homes and mean the circuit likely has no ground wire. A cheap three-prong adapter doesn't change that, and swapping in a three-prong outlet without a ground just hides it. Safer options: have an electrician add GFCI protection (labeled properly) or run a ground. A plug-in tester shows what you have. More checks by build year in Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: two prong outlets, ungrounded outlets, old house wiring, older home problems, electrical safety, house built in

Title: Spring Home Maintenance — the After-Winter Walk-Around
Description: Once the snow is gone, take a slow walk around the outside of your house. Look up at the roof and gutters for loose or missing shingles and sagging sections. Check caulk around windows and doors, peeling paint, cracked steps and walkways, and the soil along the foundation. Make a list and fix the small things before spring rains. More seasonal checklists on Walter's page.
Keywords: spring home maintenance, spring checklist, exterior home check, after winter, home maintenance tips, roof inspection

Title: 5 Home Checks That Take Under 5 Minutes Each
Description: Quick home maintenance checks anyone can do today: press TEST on your GFCI outlets, hold the furnace filter up to the light, put food coloring in the toilet tank to find a silent leak, look under every sink for drips, and test the garage door's auto-reverse. Small checks that catch problems early. Want 25 of them in one go? Get Walter's free Weekend Home Check — 25 things in 30 minutes.

Title: Seal Gaps Where Pipes and Wires Enter Your House
Description: Walk around the outside of your house and look wherever something goes through the wall: hose faucets, AC lines, cable and phone wires, dryer vents, gas and electric lines. Gaps around them let in water, drafts, insects and mice. Seal small gaps with exterior caulk and larger ones with the right foam or a cover plate. An easy exterior home maintenance walk-around. More outside checks on Walter's page.
Keywords: seal gaps, exterior caulk, pest prevention, drafty house, home maintenance tips, exterior home check

Title: Why a Sewer Camera Inspection Is Worth It on an Older Home
Description: Many older homes have clay or cast-iron sewer lines running out to the street. Tree roots, cracks and sags happen out of sight, and a standard home inspection doesn't see inside the pipe. A sewer scope (camera inspection) by a plumber shows the line's condition before you buy. Slow drains and gurgling toilets are clues too. More checks for your home's age in Walter's free house-age tool.
Keywords: sewer scope inspection, sewer line, older home problems, buying an old house, home inspection, house built in

Title: Mulch and Soil Against Siding — a House Hunting Red Flag
Description: Siding and trim should sit a few inches above the soil and mulch. When dirt is piled right against them, wood stays wet and insects have an easy way in. At a showing, look at the bottom of the siding and gently press the lowest trim boards and door frames. Soft or crumbly wood is worth pointing out to your home inspector. More buyer red flags on Walter's Home Check.
Keywords: wood rot, siding damage, termite signs, buying a house tips, house hunting checklist, home inspection

Title: Spring AC Prep — Give Your Outdoor Unit Room to Breathe
Description: Before the first hot day, look at your outdoor AC unit. Clear leaves and debris, trim plants back a couple of feet, and check that it sits level. Change the indoor filter, then run the AC for a while on a warm day to make sure it cools. Odd noises or warm air? Schedule service before the summer rush. Title: 6 Things to Ask About When Buying an Older Home
Description: Buying or living in an older house? Things worth asking about, depending on when it was built: lead paint (before 1978), asbestos in materials like old tiles and pipe wrap, knob-and-tube wiring, aluminum wiring (roughly mid-60s to mid-70s), galvanized or polybutylene pipes, and the condition of the sewer line.
